key_insight: Cu feedstock morphology governs impact deformation in cold-sprayed Cu–Al₂O₃ composites: spherical particles localize strain at splat interfaces, while spongy particles distribute strain through collapsing ligaments.
engineering_relevance: Feedstock morphology provides a design lever alongside spray parameters for tailoring ceramic encapsulation, microstructure, and deposit mechanical performance.
method: Compare spherical and spongy Cu feedstocks in cold-sprayed Cu–Al₂O₃ deposits.
Characterize microstructure and nano- and micro-hardness.
Evaluate mechanical and wear behavior using micro-compression and tribological tests.
evidence_signal: Multiscale characterization links spherical Cu to bimodal grain structures that balance strength and ductility, and spongy Cu to distributed strain hardening and enhanced ceramic encapsulation.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative performance gains or processing window, limiting assessment of effect size and transferability.
paper_title: Feedstock morphology governs impact-induced deformation in cold sprayed metal-ceramic composites
